Two conditional keys, and neither is legal on every graph: {{agentName}} resolves ONLY where the graph's TEXT sender is a marketing campaign, and a contact CUSTOM FIELD — addressable as {{ContactTag_<uuid>}}, where the uuid is a CUSTOM-FIELD id from listContactCustomFields and NOT a tag id from searchContactTags, however much the prefix suggests otherwise (ContactTag is the table that stores tags, lists and custom fields alike, so the GRN is named for the table rather than for the thing; a real tag id passes the shape check, is accepted by promote, and renders empty) — resolves ONLY on CONTACT and APPOINTMENT graphs, the ones a send loads contact context for — and on an APPOINTMENT graph only from the TEXT REMINDER, which renders with the task, the contact and the user. An appointment Slack post loads the task alone, so every CONTACT key there, tags included, renders literally even though promote accepts it: the gate judges per DOMAIN, and this is the one place a domain is wider than one of its own nodes. Used outside its condition either one is unrenderable and blocks promote exactly like an unknown key.Triggers are managed through the `triggers` array: each entry is upserted by its id (mint a fresh UUID to add one) and entries omitted from the array are detached; only `config` syncs (`name` is cosmetic). Trigger config shapes: {type: "manual"}, {type: "created"}, {type: "mutation", filter: <FilterGroup>}, {type: "match", filter: <FilterGroup>}; CONTACT-only: {type: "inbound_text", twilioPhoneNumberIds: [...]}, {type: "inbound_email", connectedAccountIds?: [...]}; EVENT workflows have exactly one trigger shape, {type: "event_received"} — the workflow's minted webhook URL is the trigger. Minimal valid drip example (node/edge shape): nodes: [{id:"n1",type:"trigger",config:{}}, {id:"n2",type:"text_action",config:{mode:"single",textBody:"Hi {{firstName}}"}}, {id:"n3",type:"wait",config:{mode:"fixed",seconds:172800,interruptEnabled:false,interruptFilter:{id:"f1",operator:"AND",conditions:[],groups:[]}}}, {id:"n4",type:"end",config:{}}], edges: [{id:"e1",config:{},parentNodeId:"n1",childNodeId:"n2"}, {id:"e2",config:{},parentNodeId:"n2",childNodeId:"n3"}, {id:"e3",config:{},parentNodeId:"n3",childNodeId:"n4"}]. PROMOTE GOTCHA: a template-less TEXT/EMAIL draft starts with communicationConfig.sender {type: "UNSET"}, and promoteWorkflowDraft rejects SenderNotChosen — set a real sender in the automation config (e.g. {type: "POINT_PERSON"}) before promoting; getWorkflow.draftValidation names this and any other blocking issues. GRAPH CONFIG — `graph.config`, the settings an operator asks for by name. It sits beside `nodes`/`edges`/`triggers` and is NOT per-node. Shared keys (every domain): `triggerOperator` "AND"|"OR" (whether a graph with several triggers needs all of them or any one); `activation.triggerEligibleRecordsNow` (on activation, enroll records that ALREADY match, not just future ones); and `triggerWindow`, which limits when ENROLLMENT may happen; `exclusiveEnrollment` true means a record entering THIS workflow is unenrolled from every OTHER workflow it is still running under — those runs are STOPPED at the moment this one is created (other WORKFLOW, so a prior version of this same workflow is left alone), which is how "only one campaign at a time per lead" is expressed. It is inert on EVENT graphs, whose runs anchor on a webhook payload rather than a record. CONTACT graphs add `exitConditions.exitConditionTypes` — any of "any_inbound_communication", "inbound_text", "inbound_email", "contact_archived" — which is how "stop the drip as soon as they reply" is expressed; there is no per-node way to say it. APPOINTMENT graphs accept the `exitConditions` key but it carries nothing (typed `undefined`), so exit conditions are effectively CONTACT-only. `communicationConfig` is NOT contact-only: CONTACT and APPOINTMENT graphs both take it, and it is where an appointment reminder's quiet hours and sender live too. SEND WINDOW — `sendWindow` (on communicationConfig) and `triggerWindow` (top level) are the same shape: {timezone, daysOfWeek?:["MON".."SUN"], startTime?:{hour,minute}, endTime?:{hour,minute}, timezoneMode?:"RECIPIENT"|"CONFIGURED"}. `hour` AND `minute` are BOTH REQUIRED on each time — {hour:9} alone is rejected by the graph parser. These are clock times, not offsets, so "weekdays 9-6 Central" is daysOfWeek MON..FRI with startTime {hour:9,minute:0} and endTime {hour:18,minute:0}. A channel that configures NOTHING is not unrestricted: it falls back to 08:00-21:00 Eastern, the TCPA envelope. Say that rather than implying a missing window means any hour. `timezoneMode` says WHOSE clock those times are read on, and it changes when a message actually goes out: "RECIPIENT" (the default, and what an omitted field means) reads them in each recipient's own zone, derived from their phone number's area code — 9:00 means 9:00 where the lead is, so one schedule fires at a different instant per contact. "CONFIGURED" reads them in the window's own `timezone` for everybody, which is what an operator means by "send on MY schedule"; it is honoured only where a recipient zone exists to differ from (TEXT), and it never sends outside 08:00-21:00 in the recipient's local time — quiet hours still floor it. EMAIL has no area code to derive a zone from and always reads the configured `timezone`, so `timezoneMode` is inert there; so is a `triggerWindow`, which gates ENROLLMENT and has no recipient. SENDER — `communicationConfig` selects who a message comes FROM, and a mode name alone is not a valid sender: most modes carry required fields. TEXT: {type:"UNSET"} | {type:"POINT_PERSON"} | {type:"MEETING_OWNER"} (appointment graphs) | {type:"PHONE", fromPhoneNumberId} | {type:"RANDOM_PHONE", fromPhoneNumberIds:[...]} | {type:"LOCAL_PRESENCE", scope, fallback} — LOCAL_PRESENCE picks a team number whose area code matches the recipient, and BOTH scope and fallback are required: scope is {kind:"ALL_TEAM"} | {kind:"SPECIFIC", fromPhoneNumberIds} | {kind:"EXCLUDE", excludedPhoneNumberIds} | {kind:"MARKETING_CAMPAIGN", ...}, and a MARKETING_CAMPAIGN scope accepts ONLY the {type:"SCOPE_POOL"} fallback. EMAIL: {type:"UNSET"} | {type:"POINT_PERSON"} | {type:"IDENTITY", fromEmail, fromClientId} | {type:"RANDOM_IDENTITY", identities:[...]}. UNSET is the creation default and activation is GATED on replacing it, so a graph left on UNSET will not run. SYSTEM CATEGORY — the separate `systemCategory` variable, not part of the graph. CONTACT, DEAL, EVENT and APPOINTMENT all allow CUSTOM workflows, so `null` is correct there — do NOT attach a category to make an appointment reminder. PROPERTY is the one domain that allows no custom workflow at all: it MUST carry "PROPERTY_SIGNAL_SKIP_TRACE", and creating one without a category is rejected with "Custom workflows are not available for property — pick a template." A non-null `systemCategory` ALSO requires a `templateId` on the same create — "A system-category workflow needs a template id" — so a category alone still fails. Both rejections read as "property workflows are not supported" if you do not know the pair is required. One category exists that NO domain offers at create time: "APPOINTMENT_REMINDER" is a stored value you may READ on an existing workflow, but nothing lists it as creatable, so never pass it on a create — the appointment domain takes custom workflows instead.

## Call

```ts
const result = await client.workflows.updateWorkflowGraph({ workflowAutomationId: '<id>', workflowGraph: <SuperJSON> }, { idempotencyKey: crypto.randomUUID() })
// → Promise<UpdateWorkflowGraphMutation>
```

`<TypeName>` placeholders are pseudocode — the field-level shape of every input and of `UpdateWorkflowGraphMutation` is TypeScript, in `dist/generated/operationTypes.d.ts`.

## Variables

| Name | Type | Required | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workflowAutomationId` | `ID!` | yes | — |
| `workflowGraph` | `SuperJSON!` | yes | — |

## Gateway notes

- Idempotent: pass `options.idempotencyKey` (e.g. a UUID) so retries can never double-fire the side effect.
- Org-guarded: the gateway verifies the ids you pass belong to your organization before executing (403 otherwise).

## Response shape

The field tree of the exact selection set the gateway executes (leaf → `true`); the resolved `result` matches it.

        }
